AheadDayOut.title: AheadDayOut

DeckCardStateOut.description: A review card of a game, for "What slipped past you" (watch.deck_cards).
DeckCardStateOut.title: DeckCardStateOut

DeckOut.description:
A practice session's state and its next item (`card`, `threat_item`,
`unannounced_item` or `puzzle`; none when today's are done).
DeckOut.title: DeckOut

ExtraWatchOut.description: An extra watch's progress, and the extra watches kept tonight (this one once done).
ExtraWatchOut.title: ExtraWatchOut

FirstStarOut.description: Before any star: the held move closest to stopping slipping (path.first_star).
FirstStarOut.title: FirstStarOut

HeldOut.description: What a watch held: answers right, answers wrong and moves that stopped slipping.
HeldOut.title: HeldOut

JourneyMapOut.description: The Progress map and the home path (GET /api/journey).

KeptNightOut.description: A kept night's watch (GET /api/journey/night): its moves and where each stands now.
KeptNightOut.title: KeptNightOut

A lesson's intro (intros.payload): the demonstration played out from the wall and the
guided first position, each in a puzzle's shape (fen_prev, prev_uci, fen_before, color,

OverviewOut.description:
Only `skill_shape` and `game_trend` are typed so far; the other overview fields pass
through as they are.

PathHistoryOut.description: Every kept night, oldest first (night N is the Nth), and every finished extra watch.

PatternCountOut.description: A tactic's tagged moves in the range, by label (blunder, mistake, miss and any other).

ReviewMarkOut.description: A stored review mark (StepMarkIn when it was saved).

SlipsOut.description:
A game's moves that slipped past (its review cards) by where they are on the watch

TodayOut.description: Today's goal, with the daily review's plan, streak and memory (daily.py).

TonightCardOut.description: A move row on the Watch page's tonight card (watch.tonight).

WardLessonOut.description: One lesson of a ward, and whether the learner is holding it.
WardLessonOut.title: WardLessonOut

A section of the curriculum. `state` is "cleared", "current", "ahead", or "blocked"
when the ward's drills do not exist yet -- blocked never clears and never blocks.

WatchOut.description: When the learner keeps their watch, the habit it follows, and the day it was saved.

WeekOut.description: The last seven days of games for the Games summary card; hidden while `analysed` is 0.
WeekOut.title: WeekOut

delete.description:
Delete you and everything of yours, right away (the web app then deletes the Clerk
account, and Clerk's user.deleted webhook would do this again, harmlessly).

get.description: The admin page: the job queue and everyone's usage.

What the web app needs before it renders: whether to sign in with Clerk, and with
which (public) key, and who to write to. Read at runtime, so one build serves staging and production.

Tonight's watch: the deck's counts and the watch's next item, by its job in the
watch's mix (mix.py): a review card, a threat question, a "Your move" or a puzzle (all
null once the watch is done). Adds cards for newly analysed games first, so the deck
is always current. `mode=extra` continues tonight's extra watch, the same mix (POST
/api/lesson/extra starts one; 409 before that).
Poll a worker-prepared map; never run Stockfish or grade a card here.

post.description: The move behind the two-step Hint: the piece to move, then the arrow.

Learn more: once today's queue is finished, raise today's new-position limit by
one pace's worth (fewer when the deck has fewer), for today only (deck.learn_more).
`added` is 0 when there was nothing to add.

Don't show this again: hide a card with a reason, keeping its schedule and history.
No grade is recorded. Hiding a hidden card changes nothing.

get.description: Hidden positions, most recently hidden first, for Progress's list.

schema.title: Response Deck Suspended Api Deck Suspended Get

post.description: Show a hidden card again; its schedule resumes where it was.

get.description:
Everything Knightly keeps about you, as a zip: your games as PGN and every table
as CSV.

The games list. Search and the Filters popover narrow the whole list; the quick
filters on top (result, kpi, to_review) pick within it, and `counts` gives each quick
filter's number for the list as narrowed. `slips` is the scope: games with moves
that slipped past you, or analysed games with none (Clean).

Every move's "Why" and "Best line" at once, from the lines the game's analysis
stored (and any deeper ones computed on demand), so review opens them without a
request per tap. Moves analysed before lines were stored are left out; the app asks
for those one at a time.

schema.title: Response Game Lines Api Games  Game Id  Lines Get

get.description:
The "Why" and "Best line" for one move: from the game's stored analysis when it
has them, else computed with Stockfish (about a second, at depth 18, counted
against the engine quota) and served from the engine_lines table after that.

post.description:
Marks a game reviewed ("Finish review"), with how each lesson step went for the
summary's marks. Finishing again moves the time forward and replaces the marks. Also
makes sure the game's positions are in the review deck, so the summary can say so.

get.description:
Home: today's goal and the journey. Today's game is your newest analysed game you
haven't reviewed, played after the newest one you have (and in the last NEW_GAME_DAYS
days).

The Progress map: stars (dimmed while their card has lapsed), ranks with the post
that reaches each and the day it was reached, and nights kept with their milestones;
for the home path, the week ahead by the cards' due dates, every kept night and extra
watch with what it held, and the first star's progress.

A kept night's watch on the path: what it held and where each of its moves stands
now. 404 for a night that was not kept.

post.description:
Start tonight's next extra watch, or resume the open one, and serve it as
`/api/deck?mode=extra` does: another watch the size of tonight's, in the same mix,
never a card answered tonight (extra.py). As many as the learner wants. `extra` is its
progress and how many extra watches were kept tonight. 409 until tonight's lesson is
finished; it never keeps the night or the streak.

get.description: A lesson's intro, to replay it from its post's card.

post.description: The learner has seen a lesson's intro: the watch stops offering it.

get.description: A public account, before adding it: the welcome flow's "Is this you?".

Who's signed in, as the app needs it: whether to show the admin page, and the
limits that apply to them.

The welcome flow's import screen: how far the first update has got, what it has
found so far, and (once the newest games are in) the summary for "Your first lesson
is ready".

What your mistakes come down to (patterns.py): how many of your blunders, mistakes
and misses in rated games in the range carry each tactic, most common first.

post.description:
Test out of the current post (or resume the open test) and serve it as
`/api/deck?mode=challenge` does: PAGE positions from its lessons at its own
difficulty. PAGE_RIGHT or more right clears the post, unless a lesson's games say not
yet (challenge.py). 409 when the post has nothing to test.
Check a practice puzzle answer move by move; the first finished try is recorded.
The move for the puzzle's current step, for the two-step Hint.
Free review exploration: a legal history, one bounded Stockfish preview.

put.description:
How many new review positions a day (Light, Standard, Intense). Today's queue
follows it at once; positions already answered today still count.

The user's time zone, which decides when their review day starts: daily counts,
due positions and the day answers are checked against. The app sends the device's.

The learner's watch: the local time they keep it and the habit it follows
("After I finish dinner"). Reminders use both; saving restarts their back-off.

get.description:
The sidebar's account row: your accounts with their latest rating, and the daily
update's state (the run in progress, else the last one).

Each day's streak state from `from` to `to` inclusive (at most 42 days,
ending no later than your today), as in Today's `streak.week`, for the streak calendar.

post.description:
Judge a "Your move" answer like a card's first move; logged, never scheduled.
The result has a card answer's shape plus its `unannounced` kind.

Queue an update (jobs.py); a worker picks it up within seconds. Asking while one
is waiting or running changes nothing.
